tex_content.html:
Theorem
[Derivation of Hamilton's ODE] ↗ thm:euler-lagrange-equations ↗ def:hamiltonian-from-lagrangian 1. ch3:3.3-thm-2\group Calculus of Variations

The pair $(x,p)$ satisfies \[ \dot x=D_pH(p,x),\qquad \dot p=-D_xH(p,x), \] and $H(p(s),x(s))$ is constant in $s$.

Proof

\sketch Differentiating $H=p\cdot q-L(q,x)$ and using $p=D_qL$ gives $D_pH=q$ and $D_xH=-D_xL$. Insert $q=\dot x$ and the Euler–Lagrange equation to obtain Hamilton’s equations. Their contraction gives $\frac d{ds}H=D_pH\cdot \dot p+D_xH\cdot \dot x=0$.

□
